papers.title: Antibacterial and pro-osteointegrative bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces for oromaxillofacial applications: a systematic review and bayesian network meta-analysis of preclinical studies
papers.abstract: Numerous preclinical studies have investigated bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces to enhance antibacterial and osteointegrative performance in oromaxillofacial applications. However, these studies employ heterogeneous experimental methods and biological outcomes, making it difficult to identify which coating strategies hold the greatest translational potential. This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to rank titanium coating strategies published over the last five years according to their biological performance, using a quantitative statistical framework. Nine coating categories of increasing compositional complexity, ranging from single-component (inorganic, organic, peptides/growth factors) to two-component and three-component formulations combining these classes with each other or with antibiotics, were compared across six biological outcomes in preclinical models. Inclusion criteria followed the PICOS framework for studies published between 2020 and 2025. Three databases were searched according to PRISMA 2020 and its NMA extension. Mean difference (MD) was used for outcomes on a common scale; ratio of means (RoM) when measurement units were heterogeneous. Treatment ranking was estimated using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Study reporting quality and data completeness were assessed, and studies with insufficient quantitative data were excluded from the quantitative synthesis. Of 143 records identified, 59 met the inclusion criteria and 40 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. SUCRA rankings indicated that three-component hybrid coatings incorporating antibiotics achieved the highest antibacterial performance and osseointegration, while inorganic coatings functionalized with peptides or growth factors demonstrated superior osteogenic differentiation. Organic coatings combined with peptides or growth factors showed the greatest cell proliferation. These findings provide the first evidence-based ranking of bioactive coating strategies for titanium implant surfaces, suggesting a potential advantage of multi-component formulations over single-agent approaches across biological outcomes. The identified compositional complexity gradient may inform the rational design of future multifunctional coatings and help prioritize candidates for further preclinical and translational validation in oromaxillofacial applications.

papers.title: Biomaterials in 3D bioprinting: Design strategies, material-technique interactions, and biomedical applications
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting has emerged as a transformative approach in biomedical engineering, enabling the fabrication of complex, patient-specific constructs through layer-by-layer deposition of biomaterials and living cells. This review critically synthesizes the role of biomaterials in 3D bioprinting by comparing how material properties, fabrication techniques, and biological requirements interact to determine construct performance across different biomedical applications. Unlike many existing reviews that discuss materials, techniques, and applications separately, this review focuses on the coupled interactions between biomaterial chemistry, fabrication methods, and application-specific requirements across multiple tissue systems. Across these applications, no single biomaterial satisfies all design requirements, leading to compromises between mechanical strength, printability, and biological performance. Hard tissue applications prioritize thermoplastic polymers and ceramics for structural integrity, while soft tissue engineering relies on hydrogel-based bioinks. Printing techniques such as extrusion, inkjet, and stereolithography impose constraints related to resolution, viscosity, and cell viability, driving the use of composite biomaterials and hybrid fabrication strategies. Despite significant advances, major challenges remain, including mechanical mismatch, limited vascularization, reproducibility, and lack of long-term in vivo validation. This review highlights 4D printing, smart biomaterials, and artificial intelligence-assisted design as emerging strategies to advance clinically translatable constructs. Taken together, successful bioprinting is governed by coupled biomaterial-technique interactions within specific clinical contexts.

papers.title: Towards Sustainable Interactive Devices: A Literature Review of Biomaterials in HCI Fabrication
papers.abstract: Abstract - Biomaterials are increasingly used in HCI fabrication as alternatives to petroleum-derived substrates, offering new possibilities for low-temperature making, embodied material experiences, and end-of-life pathways that differ from conventional materials. While recent reviews have begun to map adjacent subareas (e.g., biomaterials for eTextiles and critical perspectives on living systems), the field still lacks an integrated account of biomaterials as fabrication practices across interactive systems. In this review, we synthesize prior work to connect four elements that are typically treated in isolation: the biomaterial palette used in HCI, the fabrication techniques that make these materials practicable, the ways biomaterials contribute to interactive functionality (including sensing, actuation, and degradation-mediated unmaking), and the application contexts that shape acceptable lifetimes, care demands, and end-of-life handling. By organizing the literature through these linked lenses, we provide a consolidated map of the design space, surface cross-cutting patterns, and trade-offs that recur across material families and techniques, and articulate implications for more reproducible, comparable, and operational sustainability claims in future biofabrication research.

papers.title: A review of prediction and control methods on welding-induced distortions in large metallic structures
papers.abstract: Welding enables cost-effective fabrication of large structures in shipbuilding, aerospace and automotive industries, but repeated thermal cycles during multi-stage assembly inevitably cause distortions that often exceed design tolerances, degrading structural performance and requiring costly corrections. Despite significant advances in local weld modelling, predicting distortion in large, complex assemblies remains challenging due to interactions among material properties, structural geometry, heat input, welding sequence and restraint conditions, particularly for lightweight, thin-walled high-strength steels and aluminium alloys. This review synthesises research from 2000 to 2025 to assess distortion prediction and mitigation strategies for large metallic structures, emphasising industrial applicability. Thermo-elasto-plastic finite element methods provide high accuracy but at significant computational cost and inherent strain-based approaches offer efficient large-scale simulations but rely on calibration and simplifying assumptions, while local/global methods balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Data-driven surrogate models are emerging for rapid prediction and optimisation. No single approach is universally transferable across structural configurations, with scalability generally achieved at the expense of calibration requirements and application-specific assumptions. Distortion mitigation is most effective at the design stage through welding sequence optimisation and structural planning. In-process techniques such as thermal tensioning and controlled restraint further reduce distortions, while post-welding corrections remain less efficient. The literature is strongly concentrated on conventional structural steels, with only approximately 10% and 1% of the reviewed references addressing large aluminium and high-strength steel structures, respectively. Overall, major limitations concern scalability, standardisation and data availability, highlighting the need for integrated physics-based and data-driven frameworks for efficient large-scale distortion control. papers.title: Advanced Control Strategies to Enhance Stability of DC Microgrids Islanded under Dynamic Conditions
papers.abstract: Abstract Islanding of microgrids leads to unwanted fluctuations in power, voltage, current, and frequency parameters. In this paper, a comprehensive three-level control strategy is proposed to stabilize an islanded microgrid by sending control commands to the distributed generation (DG) units based on inverters. The first level of control involves droop control, which manages the power control. The second control level ensures the stability of the voltage and frequency of the network. To implement this control level, the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) method is used for the DC converter connected to the DG unit, and the Virtual Oscillator Control (VOC) method is employed to control parallel inverters. Finally, the third control level, located at the load side, is responsible for stabilizing the power of the islanded microgrid under varying load conditions, which is implemented using a Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) controlled by Model Predictive Control (MPC). Sensitivity analysis of the proposed control model is carried out under transient conditions caused by load variations, environmental changes (changes in irradiance levels), and consequently, changes in the output power of the DG units. Simulation results in the MATLAB/Simulink environment show that the proposed control strategy can stabilize the microgrid and minimize the fluctuations of power, voltage, and frequency under various operating conditions.

papers.title: Unlocking feedforward capabilities in Model Predictive Control algorithms to deal with measurable disturbances
papers.abstract: Disturbance rejection is a central objective in process control, particularly when measurable disturbances can be exploited through feedforward action. Although Model Predictive Control (MPC) naturally incorporates disturbance models and prediction capabilities, standard formulations cannot achieve complete disturbance rejection since the cost function penalises control effort. This limitation prevents MPC from reproducing the behaviour of classical feedforward compensators. This work proposes a novel framework to embed true feedforward capabilities within MPC without removing the control effort penalty. The approach introduces a dual-control structure in which two control actions are computed simultaneously: a tracking-oriented action addressing set-point tracking and robustness, and a feedforward-oriented action dedicated to disturbance rejection. Both contributions are combined into a single control signal on which the process constraints are explicitly enforced. The feedforward-oriented action is formulated without penalising control effort, enabling full compensation of measurable disturbances. The methodology is developed for Dynamic Matrix Control (DMC), Generalised Predictive Control (GPC), and state-space MPC. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through simulation studies, including comparisons with standard MPC and classical feedforward schemes. A case study based on a reverse osmosis process shows that the proposed approach improves disturbance rejection while preserving constraint handling and overall control performance.

papers.title: Suction drainage is associated with early hemoglobin decline without detectable clinical benefit after total joint arthroplasty: a propensity score–matched study
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate the impact of routine postoperative suction drainage on perioperative outcomes following primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) using a propensity score–matched cohort. Methods A retrospective cohort study included 2,339 consecutive patients who underwent primary THA or TKA between January 2020 and May 2026. Patients were categorized according to postoperative suction drain use. Propensity score matching using age, sex, and body mass index, with exact matching for procedure type, yielded 630 matched pairs (1,260 patients). Primary outcomes were postoperative hemoglobin (Hb) change and estimated blood loss (EBL). Secondary outcomes included transfusion, length of stay, and postoperative infectious, wound, and thromboembolic complications. Subgroup analyses were performed according to procedure type, antiplatelet use, and anticoagulant use. Results Following propensity score matching, the suction drain group demonstrated a greater reduction in Hb on POD1 (2.0 ± 1.0 vs. 1.8 ± 0.9 g/dL, p = 0.005), whereas Hb change on POD2 was comparable between groups. Estimated blood loss, transfusion rate, length of stay, postoperative wound complications, thromboembolic events, and acute periprosthetic joint infection were similar between groups. Procedure-specific subgroup analyses demonstrated generally consistent findings in both THA and TKA. Among patients receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant medications, postoperative hemoglobin decline, estimated blood loss, transfusion rate, and length of stay were comparable between the suction drain and no-suction drain groups. Conclusions Routine suction drain use following primary total joint arthroplasty was primarily associated with early postoperative laboratory differences, without meaningful differences in clinically relevant perioperative outcomes. Level of Evidence: Retrospective cohort study, Level Ⅲ

papers.title: Effects of a Flipped Classroom Approach on Grade 6 Learners' Achievement in Marcotting: A Quasi-Experimental Study in Philippine Technology and Livelihood Education
papers.abstract: Technology and Livelihood Education (TLE) is a key element of education in the Philippines, aiming to provide learners with the skills, knowledge, and work attitude needed for daily life and careers (Barcelona et al., 2023; Valle & Valle, 2024). At the elementary level, TLE introduces pupils to agriculture, plant propagation, home economics, and entrepreneurship so they can understand basic livelihood competencies before taking specialized courses in junior and senior high school. The purpose of the revised education program under the MATATAG Curriculum (Department of Education [DepEd], 2024) has been repeated, making the classes focused on the learners, stressing the competencies, and considering local realities. In many classes in the Philippines, TLE is still taught mainly in traditional ways. Teachers conduct lectures, explain, and demonstrate as if they had little time for hands-on practice and face issues such as time limitations as well as difficulties with facilities and lack of training (Barcelona et al., 2023; Espiritu, 2022). This limited peer learning becomes especially problematic when teaching procedures like marcotting (i.e., a specific type of plant reproduction in which branches are attached to the parent plant) (Hartmann et al., 2014).To learn how to conduct marcotting, students must grasp several processes, such as selecting a suitable branch, girdling and stripping the bark, applying a damp rooting medium (including rooting hormone, if available), wrapping and securing the medium, monitoring, and separating the rooted branch. When students have little time left to practice these operations under the teacher's supervision, because the lesson is spent discussing each stage in detail, the tension can be resolved by using the Flipped Classroom model. Flipped Classroom alters the way knowledge is conveyed by shifting its transmission to the time outside of class when brief instructional videos and study materials are used. Classroom time is then available for active, collaborative, and hands-on learning under teacher supervision (Abeysekera & Dawson, 2015; Bergmann & Sams, 2012). According to meta-analyses made on flipping, the approach is indeed effective and shows reasonable evolutionary diversity, but the studies are mostly conducted in the higher education sector and school learning, and there is little data about utilization of the flipped approach among learners of the upper elementary school stage, who are less experienced in planning their own education (Lo & Hew, 2017). This gap has practical and theoretical implications. Practically, TLE teachers need to ensure that their efforts to find appropriate materials are reasonable and satisfactory for students, given differences in home devices and internet access. From the theoretical standpoint, the content of TLE, such as cases on marcotting, serves as a perfect material for testing the argument made by many scholars claiming that the mechanism of flipping leads to better learning because it allows students to dedicate class time to guided performance of certain tasks under the supervision of the teacher (Abeysekera & Dawson, 2015; Mayer, 2021). The present study therefore examined the effect of a four-week flipped classroom approach on Grade 6 learners’ achievement in marcotting, compared with conventional lecture-discussion instruction. Specifically, it addressed four research questions: 1. What were the pre-test achievement levels of the experimental (flipped) and comparison (conventional) classes in marcotting, and were the two classes comparable at baseline? 2. What were the post-test achievement levels of the two classes after four weeks of instruction? 3. Was there a significant change from pre-test to post-test within each class? 4. Was there a significant difference in post-test achievement between the two classes, and how large was the difference? Two null hypotheses were tested at the .05 level of significance. H₀₁: There is no significant difference between the pre-test and post-test achievement of learners within either class. H₀₂: There is no significant difference in post-test achievement between learners taught through the flipped classroom approach and those taught through conventional instruction. Review of Related Literature The Flipped Classroom: Definition and Evidence Base The flipped classroom method reverses established norms regarding teaching. The first introduction to a topic is done before students enter the classroom (usually through videos created or shared by the instructor), and time in class is now dedicated only to activities that encourage learners to assimilate, collaborate, and use the information received (Bergmann & Sams, 2012; Bishop & Verleger, 2013). Tomas et al. (2019) point out that flipping is not a means but a continuum of instruments whose efficacy hinges on learners' preparedness and the ability to connect pre-class and in-class activities. Similarly, Deng et al. (2022) argue that flipped learning should be viewed as student-centered, but as a refined practice rather than simply introducing videos into teaching. According to some studies, flipped classrooms can be said to be effective since meta-analyses carried out in various areas show that learners achieve moderate gains (g = 0.19; Cheng et al., 2019) and substantial gains (g = 0.36, van Alten et al., 2019; g = 0.50, Strelan et al., 2020), but the results vary greatly across studies. The effects become more notable when in-class activities involve active learning and include checks for students’ preparation (van Alten et al., 2019). In the study conducted by Gross et al. (2015), it was claimed that the improvement in performance was largely facilitated by the increased preparation of students. Reviews of the advantages and pitfalls that flipping presents highlight students’ awareness, teachers’ workload, and access to technology as problems in the field (Akçayır & Akçayır, 2018; Kapur et al., 2022). Flipped Instruction with Younger Learners Most flipped classroom research has been conducted in higher education, and its findings cannot feasibly be applied to younger learners. In the critical review, K–12 studies by Lo and Hew (2017) reveal generally positive effects while identifying challenges specific to school settings: learners almost never watch the videos; access to devices at home is terribly limited; unfamiliarity with the approach; and the time required for teachers to produce materials. They suggested short videos and simple pre-class tasks to diagnose understanding, with in-class activities following directly from that content. In reports involving lower secondary learners, achievement and engagement increased when these were in place (Ying & Ayub, 2022), and research on blended learning with Grade 6 students indicates that learners' self-regulation and access to resources shape outcomes (Nguyen et al., 2024). Taken together, the findings suggest that upper elementary learners will benefit from flipping only when the pre-class component is short, readily available, and closely linked to classroom tasks. Flipped Instruction in Technical, Vocational, and Philippine Contexts Data from studies on technical and vocational education are important for TLE. Holik (2019) investigated how the flipping process affected students' performance and engagement in a cooking program in CTE and concluded that it increased performance and class involvement because students arrived in class after seeing the process performed first and were ready to master the procedure in the lab. Research in other subjects that focus on skills learned through demonstration has also shown that watching videos on the topic before the lesson improves students' performance and learning (Elmaadaway, 2018). In the Philippines, studies on flipped learning in chemistry (Macale et al., 2021) and biology (Malto et al., 2018) showed improvements in students' performance and learners' feelings in college education (Gonzales, 2019). Researchers investigating TLE call for an innovative approach to developing technical skills (Barcelona et al., 2023), the use of supportive videos and electronic materials (Espiritu, 2022; Grandeza & Grandeza, 2024), and differentiated, inclusive methods (Mendoza, 2024). Related intervention studies in classrooms in the Philippines show that applying a well-structured, student-centered approach, such as peer reading, can improve performance for many students in a short time and achieve a large effect size. Student feedback indicates that program length and the alignment of activities with assessments should be considered when designing such programs (Astrero & Eugenio, 2025). However, to date, no study has tested flipped classroom in agriculture or plant propagation. Synthesis and Research Gap In this study's conclusion, three gaps are highlighted. Research on the flipped classroom concept has mainly focused on post-secondary education and academic subjects, neglecting elementary vocational training and education. Second, only some studies focus on procedural subjects, where flipping provides the most help because it gives students time to practice. Lastly, many articles report only the significance level of an experiment, not effect sizes. This research addresses these gaps by reviewing the flipped classroom model in marcotting for 6th-grade students and reporting impact measures alongside experimental results. papers.title: Grape Cluster Inspired Biomimetic Composite Solid Electrolyte for High‐Voltage and Long‐Life Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state lithium metal batteries suffer from poor interfacial stability and dendrite growth, primarily limited by the ion transport kinetics and mechanical properties of composite solid electrolytes (CSE). Inspired by the hierarchical grape cluster, we design a biomimetic electrolyte via electrospinning PAN fiber “pedicel” integrated with mesoporous SiO 2 ‐SO 3 Li “grape berry” fillers, followed by in‐situ polymerization. This structure establishes long‐range Li + conduction channels and a robust physical barrier, delivering a high Li + transference number of 0.65, ionic conductivity of 1.44 × 10 −3 S cm −1 at 25°C, and a modulus of 520 MPa. Benefiting from these advantages, the assembled LFP|Li and NCM811|Li cells achieve 88.8% capacity retention after 1000 cycles and 94.3% after 300 cycles, respectively. Moreover, a high‐loading pouch cell realizes an energy density of 414.9 Wh kg −1 /797.8 Wh L −1 and withstands harsh abuse tests. Mechanistically, DFT and phase‐field simulations reveal the dual Li + pathways and TFSI − immobilization enabled by the ‐SO 3 Li groups. Notably, a physics‐informed neural network (PINN) framework decouples interface activation‐aging kinetics and predicts long‐term impedance evolution. This work provides a biomimetic paradigm and data‐driven methods for the design and interface analysis of high‐performance CSE.

papers.title: A comprehensive simulation framework for evaluating U.S. lung allocation policies
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapidly evolving landscape of lung allocation policy, including the recent adoption of the Continuous Distribution framework, demands simulation tools that are both flexible and computationally efficient. Existing lung allocation simulators are often difficult to adapt to new policy designs and can be computationally burdensome when large numbers of replications are needed for uncertainty quantification and optimization. This paper introduces the Modular Lung Allocation Policy Simulation Model (MoLAPS), a high-fidelity, discrete-event simulation framework designed to address these limitations through a modular policy architecture and parallel execution. MoLAPS integrates detailed patient and donor data, dynamic medical status updates, and a predictive organ-offer acceptance model. It is implemented with parallel computing support, substantially reducing runtimes for multi-replication and longer-horizon experiments and enabling the exploration of large-scale policy design spaces. The model features a modular architecture that isolates policy components, including allocation, acceptance, and prioritization rules, allowing policymakers to easily evaluate existing and proposed allocation policies, or hypothetical alternatives. A surrogate-based calibration procedure aligns simulation outputs with national organ transplant data, improving empirical validity. MoLAPS is rigorously validated using prediction intervals, quantile-quantile plots, and Chi-squared tests. Simulation results closely align with real-world data across key performance indicators, including transplant rates, waitlist mortality, and organ nonuse. MoLAPS provides clinicians, policymakers, and researchers with a timely, open, and extensible platform for policy evaluation. By enabling realistic, data-driven assessments of lung allocation strategies, it supports more equitable, efficient, and evidence-based transplant policy decisions.

papers.abstract: This study presents an artistic herbarium specimen-making workshop as a teaching resource at the Integrated University for Older Adults (UNITI/UFMA), grounded in active learning methodologies that value older adults’ active participation and cultural background. The methodology consisted of collecting and herborizing plant structures, followed by the creation of original artistic herbarium specimens through collages and drawings. The results demonstrated the engagement and autonomy of older adults in creating botanical compositions, as well as the application of knowledge related to the recognition and differentiation of plant structures, the use of botanical terminology, and the association of this knowledge with previous experiences and affective memories. Each artistic herbarium specimen carries symbolism linked to the students’ lived experiences, representing memories and identities while valuing personal and collective narratives. It is concluded that integrating different fields of knowledge into the teaching and learning of botany contributes to cognitive and social development, transforming scientific documentation into an object of social connection that respects and values the sensitivity and life histories of older adults.

papers.title: Bayesian Deep Reliability Network for dynamic human reliability analysis in high-risk industrial environments
papers.abstract: Abstract Industrial and mining accidents continue to pose significant threats to worker safety and production operations worldwide, with human error accounting for a substantial proportion of high-risk incidents. This paper addresses three critical challenges in contemporary Human Reliability Analysis (HRA): the inability of traditional methods to capture dynamic human-machine-environment interactions, the difficulty in integrating heterogeneous multi-source data, and the lack of interpretable uncertainty quantification in deep learning predictions. To tackle these issues, we propose the Bayesian Deep Reliability Network (BDRN), a novel framework that integrates a Graph Attention Temporal Encoder (GATE) for spatiotemporal dependency modeling, a Multimodal Feature Fusion Network (MFFN) for heterogeneous data integration, and an Evidential Deep Reinforcement Learning (EDRL) module for uncertainty-aware decision support. The proposed model is validated on the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) accident dataset and the New York City Motor Vehicle Collisions dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that BDRN achieves superior performance with an accuracy of 0.892, F1-score of 0.867, and AUC-ROC of 0.921 on the MSHA dataset, numerically higher than traditional Bayesian network HRA models, LSTM-based sequence models, and Transformer-based classifiers. Furthermore, the uncertainty calibration error of 0.068 confirms the model’s reliability in quantifying decision confidence. This research bridges the gap between probabilistic reasoning and deep learning, providing a practical tool for safety decision-making in high-risk industrial environments.

papers.title: Spatially Programmed 3D‐Bioprinted Tumor–Stromal Assembloids Reveal Progressive Microenvironmental Remodeling and Phase‐Dependent Drug Responses in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatocellular csarcinoma (HCC) progression is driven by dynamic interactions between cancer cells and stromal fibroblasts that evolve with spatial proximity and physical association. However, conventional co‐culture models either combine these populations from the outset or maintain them in permanent separation, limiting compartment‐specific analysis of their progressive interaction. Here, we develop a distance‐programmed tumor–stromal assembloid platform in which tumor and stromal microtissues are bioprinted at defined surface‐to‐surface separations. We engineer a collagen–alginate hybrid bioink that restrains spreading, promotes cell–cell cohesion, and preserves discrete tumor and stromal compartments throughout assembly, while interface angle and neck length quantify structural integration, which TGF‐β1 accelerates. Compartment‐specific tracking resolves a graded E‐cadherin‐to‐N‐cadherin transition within the tumor compartment together with progressive activation and spatial expansion of the stromal compartment. Paracrine signaling, fibroblast activation, matrix remodeling, and drug‐resistance programs predominate at distinct phases, producing phase‐dependent responses to pathway‐specific inhibition combined with doxorubicin. Modular repetition of these units extends assembly across a large spatial field, yielding an interconnected centimeter‐scale array with high viability. This platform couples compartment‐resolved analysis of tumor–stromal remodeling with a scalable route to macroscale tumor tissues.
